purpose: Second robust domain attempt (domain 2 of 2 required) for wavelet-multiresolution-scaling, alongside the already-verified domain 1 (seismology / Tohoku 2011, USGS/GCMT label). Physiology (CHF vs NSR) and network traffic (Bellcore) attempts in this line had weak (class-comparison, not temporal-transition) or unverified labels; this record instead uses a genuine WITHIN-RECORD temporal transition (interictal -> ictal) of a single continuous signal from a single patient, clinically annotated onset/offset -- structurally analogous to the PhysioNet SDDB VF-onset label and the Tohoku mainshock label used elsewhere in this line.
prohibition_note: Golden rule of this lab: no fabricated data/citations/URLs/results. Every URL, byte count, and HTTP status below was obtained by an actual curl request in this session (agent proxy environment); the EDF binary was parsed byte-for-byte in this session with a from-scratch parser (no pyedflib/mne available in the environment), not copied from a library example or fabricated.

dataset.source_description: Pediatric intractable-epilepsy scalp EEG recordings, Children's Hospital Boston / MIT, 23 cases (22 subjects), continuous multi-hour .edf files per case, seizure onset/offset annotated by the clinical team for each recording.
dataset.license: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0 ("Open Access" per PhysioNet content page) -- no account, login, or credentialing required. Verified by fetching all URLs below with plain unauthenticated curl (no cookies/auth headers) and getting HTTP 200.

urls_accessed.purpose: clinical seizure annotation summary (montage + per-file onset/offset in seconds)
raw continuous EEG recording containing one full seizure, downloaded in full

binary WFDB-format seizure annotation file accompanying chb01_03.edf (present, HTTP 200, 54 bytes -- confirms an annotation exists for this file; NOT decoded numerically in this session, human-readable chb01-summary.txt was used instead as the authoritative onset/offset source, which is the standard practice for this database)

cross-check: confirms chb01_03.edf is listed among the 182 seizure-containing files across the database (first entries: chb01/chb01_03.edf, chb01/chb01_04.edf, chb01/chb01_15.edf, chb01/chb01_16.edf, chb01/chb01_18.edf, chb01/chb01_21.edf, chb01/chb01_26.edf, ...)

dataset.note_on_deidentification: The EDF header's patient-name field literally reads 'Surrogate Name' (de-identified per IRB/PhysioNet requirements for a pediatric database, as expected). Patient identity is case chb01, 1 of 22 subjects; not a personally identifying value.

edf_header_parsed_fields.file_size_check: 6144 + 3600 records * 11776 bytes/record = 42399744 bytes, exactly matches the downloaded file size -- confirms the parser's field offsets are correct, not just plausible-looking.

dataset.channel_choice_rationale: First channel in the standard 10-20 bipolar montage used by this database. Confirmed (by fetching chb02-summary.txt, chb05-summary.txt, chb08-summary.txt in this session) that 'Channel 1: FP1-F7' and 'Data Sampling Rate: 256 Hz' are identical across at least these three other patients' summary files, i.e. this channel/rate choice is fixed and consistent across patients, not cherry-picked per-file.

transition_label.source: https://physionet.org/files/chbmit/1.0.0/chb01/chb01-summary.txt (clinical annotation file accompanying the raw EEG, produced by the CHB epilepsy monitoring unit team; not computed or embedded by us, and not derived from the wavelet/multifractal method being tested -- non-circular in the same sense as the SDDB #vfon and USGS/GCMT Tohoku labels used elsewhere in this line)
transition_label.raw_annotation: File Name: chb01_03.edf / Seizure Start Time: 2996 seconds / Seizure End Time: 3036 seconds
transition_label.meaning: Elapsed time in seconds from the start of chb01_03.edf (13:43:04) to clinically annotated seizure onset and offset, i.e. an interictal -> ictal -> (post-ictal, not yet reached within this file) transition within one continuous single-patient recording.
transition_label.structural_analogy: Same structure as PhysioNet SDDB '#vfon: 07:54:33' (ventricular fibrillation onset, used for critical-slowing-down domain 2 in this line) and as the USGS/GCMT-timed Tohoku 2011 mainshock (used for wavelet-multiresolution-scaling domain 1): an externally/clinically timestamped regime-change event inside one continuous recording of one physical system.

extraction.method: From-scratch EDF parser (no pyedflib/mne in this environment): parsed the 256-byte main header, the 23x256-byte per-signal sub-headers (labels, physical/digital min-max, samples-per-record), verified header_bytes + n_records*record_bytes == actual file size exactly, then for each of the 640 one-second data records in the extraction window read the FP1-F7 channel's 256 int16 samples, concatenated them, and linearly rescaled from digital counts to physical microvolts using (phys_max-phys_min)/(dig_max-dig_min) with dig_min=-2048, dig_max=2047, phys_min=-800 uV, phys_max=800 uV (values taken from this file's own per-signal header, not assumed).
extraction.window_definition: Seizure onset (2996s) minus 300s to seizure offset (3036s) plus 300s, i.e. 5 minutes of pre-ictal/interictal EEG before onset and 5 minutes of post-ictal EEG after offset, all from the same continuous chb01_03.edf file.
extraction.seizure_onset_index_note: index = (2996 - 2696) * 256 = 76800; index of seizure offset = (3036-2696)*256 = 87040. 0-indexed into the 'values_uV' array below.
extraction.units: microvolts (uV), physical (calibrated) values, not raw digital counts
sanity_checks_passed: exact byte-count match between parsed header/record structure and actual downloaded file size
no NaN/Inf values in extracted series
value range (-480.0 uV to 499.5 uV, mean ~0.19 uV) consistent with plausible scalp EEG amplitudes
channel label and sampling rate cross-checked against 3 other patients' summary files

series.description: time_sec_from_file_start[i] and values_uV[i] are the FP1-F7 scalp EEG voltage at 256 Hz, covering 5 minutes before through 5 minutes after the clinically annotated seizure in chb01_03.edf (patient chb01).

verdict.reasoning: The CHB-MIT database is genuinely open (Open Data Commons Attribution license, no login/credentialing, verified by unauthenticated curl returning HTTP 200 on every URL listed above), the .edf format parsed cleanly and the byte accounting matched exactly (strong evidence the extracted values are real, not corrupted or misaligned), and the seizure onset/offset timestamps come from a clinical summary file external to and independent of the wavelet/multifractal method under test -- the same non-circularity property as the domain-1 (Tohoku) label. The transition is WITHIN one continuous recording of one patient (interictal -> ictal), not a between-class/between-subject comparison, which is exactly the structural defect the Phase 0 survey flagged in the cardiac CHF-vs-NSR and Bellcore network-traffic attempts for this same candidate. This therefore looks usable as domain 2, PENDING the actual Delta(alpha)/WTMM multifractal-width computation on this series (not performed in this session -- only data acquisition, parsing, and label verification were done here, matching the scope of the equivalent domain-1 Tohoku verification and the critical-slowing-down Phase 0 domain verifications, which also stopped at data-access verification without computing Delta I).
caveats: Only ONE seizure in ONE patient (chb01_03.edf) was extracted and verified in this session; the database has 182 annotated seizures across 22 subjects, so replication across patients (needed before any preregistration) is still open.
No wavelet/WTMM/MFDFA computation of Delta(alpha) or generalized Hurst exponents was performed in this session -- this deliverable is data acquisition + label verification only, per the task scope.

Scalp EEG is a noisier, more artifact-prone signal than the Tohoku seismometer trace or SDDB ECG (eye blinks, muscle artifact, electrode movement are common in pediatric EEG) -- this was not screened for in this session; an artifact check should precede any real multifractal analysis.

The 5-minute pre/post padding around the seizure was a reasonable, not database-prescribed, choice by this agent -- a genuine preregistration would need to fix this window rule independently of any post-hoc look at the data.

Post-ictal window here is truncated to 300s after offset and does not extend to a distinct 'return to interictal baseline' marker, since the database does not annotate one; only onset/offset of the ictal event itself is clinically labeled.
